reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it explains eBay's out-of-stock option and how sellers can enable it. The speaker discusses replenishing inventory, preserving listing history, and insertion fees as operational tradeoffs rather than promising guaranteed financial returns. The description contains ordinary eBay-business resources and an explicit affiliate disclosure.

citations.quote: I get so many questions about the ebay out of stock option, what it is, why you would use it, what it does and so this video is gonna be talking about that

if an item sells and it's out of stock, if I get more of those identical items in a liquidation, I can simply go in and just add quantities to that current active listing and suddenly it's available for sale again.
From your eBay seller hub, just go up to the top left corner and click on account settings. And then you wanna go over to site preferences.
the out of stock option is probably not gonna make sense if you get a lot of unique one-off items like if you're doing thrifted items or clothing that you probably won't get again
for me it's worth it to pay the 10 cents a listing to keep it active that way if i do get more of it that sales history is still on that listing

opening.argument: The presentation links a seller action directly to an income-oriented outcome. Viewers are encouraged to enable the out-of-stock setting, while the description frames that choice as potentially producing “MORE SALES.” The speaker then reinforces the pitch by saying a listing can “sell even faster” after inventory is replenished and that eBay will want the item to sell again. This is more than neutral configuration help: it presents a simple platform setting as a route to improved sales performance, while the same description directs viewers toward stores, coaching, and numerous commercial links.

citations.quote: I could mean MORE SALES!
that item sells even faster than it did the first couple of times
For One on One Coaching Rates: [EMAIL]

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an operational tutorial does not remove the solicitation. The key message is not merely where to click; it is that maintaining a listing preserves sales history and can improve future sales. The description itself highlights “MORE SALES,” then places coaching and store links alongside the advice. A disclosure may identify affiliate compensation, but it does not establish that the sales-improvement claim is substantiated.

citations.quote: I could mean MORE SALES!
the more sales history on an eBay listing, the more search optimization that listing has
My eBay store link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The setting is explained with concrete operational details, including that it preserves an active listing and that the speaker lacks hard data for the algorithmic benefit. The phrase “MORE SALES” is promotional wording in the description, not a guaranteed reward or an instruction to pay money. Coaching and affiliate links do not show that enabling the setting is a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Of course, I have no hard data to back this up. I only have my personal experience.
you do have to pay an insertion fee to keep that listing active
Most Links you find here are affiliate and I receive a small commission off of each sale.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an easy settings change is associated with increased sales, the description uses emphatic promotional language, and viewers are offered external commercial pathways including free accounts, bonuses, referral codes, and coaching. The video also relies heavily on personal success anecdotes, such as the claim that one listing went from one or two sales a week to one or two a day. That combination can make a low-effort business tactic appear more reliably lucrative than the evidence supports, especially when the speaker concedes there is no hard data.

citations.quote: Of course, I have no hard data to back this up. I only have my personal experience.
I started selling one to two a day
get a $10 BONUS with my Referral Code: oluemq
Get Amazon Prime for half the price HERE (income limits to qualify)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary subject matter is exactly what makes the risk easy to miss: the speaker wraps an unverified ranking claim in practical seller instructions and a series of attractive commercial offers. “Personal experience” is not independent proof, and the explicit “MORE SALES” framing gives viewers a reason to act before verifying the benefit. The numerous links and referral incentives add a commercial layer that the tutorial characterization understates.

citations.quote: my listing would shoot to the top
I could mean MORE SALES!
$5 off $35+ Use Code: LINDEY5

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The account is expressly limited to personal experience rather than presented as tested proof, and the speaker also discloses the downside: inactive listings can incur insertion fees. The external offers are listed in the description, but the central video explains an eBay setting and does not require viewers to use those offers. Discounts, affiliate links, and a referral bonus do not turn seller education into a low-barrier cash-acquisition scheme.

citations.quote: during those 90 days, you do have to pay an insertion fee to keep that listing active

opening.argument: Although packaged as education, the video repeatedly steers viewers toward a business-growth narrative. The setting is presented as a way to preserve ranking advantages, bring watchers back, and make listings sell faster, while the description explicitly says the choice could mean more sales. The surrounding promotion is substantial: viewers are directed to an eBay store, one-on-one coaching, recommended products, and multiple referral offers. That makes the instructional framing functionally promotional, encouraging participation in a commercial system rather than simply explaining software.

citations.quote: there are more upsides to having the out of stock option turned on than the downsides
if you replenish that stock, that watcher will know about it and they can buy it again
For One on One Coaching Rates: [EMAIL]
Most Links you find here are affiliate and I receive a small commission off of each sale.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The promotional function is visible in the outcome-focused framing, not just in the presence of navigation steps. The audience is told the setting can preserve watchers, improve search exposure, and generate more sales, then is given commercial destinations and paid coaching contact information. Describing the mechanics accurately does not prevent the overall message from steering viewers toward a business opportunity whose central upside is asserted largely through anecdote.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video gives balanced conditions that undermine a promotional interpretation: the option is said not to fit unique one-off items, it carries continuing insertion fees, and its ranking benefit is explicitly identified as personal experience without hard data. Explaining why a seller may choose a setting, while disclosing affiliate commissions and costs, is ordinary commerce education. The links do not prove that viewers are promised a reward for clicking or registering.
